# Data source description

## Data source:

The primary dataset of this project is the Kaggle dataset [Wall Street Bets 2022](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/gpreda/wallstreetbets-2022).
The original author collected the dataset using python package `praw` daily, and
scraped the daily data from Reddit. While being named "WSB data 2022", the
actual date of post span across January 27, 2021 and March 27, 2025, give us
four years of timespan to study. For our study, we are only interested in the
*post* data along with their interaction index (points, comment number),
therefore comment data (with a title "Comment") were excluded.

The original dataset contains the following columns:

- Post title
- Post score
- Post ID
- Post URL
- Number of comments under the post
- Creation timestamp
- Post body (content)
- Timestap (in date format)

We expanded the dataset by adding sarcasm score for both post title and post
body, under column `title_sarcasm` and `body_sarcasm`. The sarcasm score was
created with the assistence of [bertweet-base-finetuned-SARC-DS](https://huggingface.co/surrey-nlp/bertweet-base-finetuned-SARC-DS),
a publicly available huggingface model trained based on self-annotated reddit
sarcasm database
[SARC](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.05579?utm_source=chatgpt.com). Posts without
body have sarcasm score 0.

The complimentary dataset we are considering might be daily stock price in NYSE,
like NASDAQ, S&P 500. We will only use these data along with comment data to
*predict* the intearction indexes.

## Assumptions:

### Assumption 1: SARC classifier reliability 

Sarcasm can be reliably detected using SARC as the training set.
The SARC training data consists of Reddit comments from 2009-2017, while the target data is r/wallstreetbets posts from 2022. 
The two differ in time period, community, and text type. Meme culture on r/wallstreetbets means its references, jokes, and sarcasm are constantly changing,
and memes are well documented to have short lifespans in online spaces. 
This matters here because many of the sarcastic references in the 2022 data did not exist in the 2009-2017 period.

## Assumption 2: Genuine human posts

While the dataset across 2021-2025 should provide us with a relatively
representative r/wallstreetbets post pattern, the conclusion might still be
biased if automatic bots represented a different posting behavior. For instance, 
within the first 100 rows or so there are a couple near-duplicate posts like two 
AST SpaceMobile satellite posts differ by a few characters. We are unable to
independently verify the geunity of data sources.


# Data loading and processing

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(data.table)
library(lubridate) # data-time package
```

Raw data loading, selecting only posts

```{r load-and-inspect-dataset, eval=FALSE}
data_wsb2022_raw = read_csv("./data/wallstreetbets_2022.csv")

data_wsb2022_raw |>
  head(5) |>
  kable()

data_wsb2022_postonly = data_wsb2022_raw |>
  filter(title != "Comment")

data_wsb2022_postonly

nrow(data_wsb2022_raw)
nrow(data_wsb2022_postonly)

data_wsb2022_postonly |>
  write_csv("./data/wsb_2022_postonly.csv")
```



```{r sarcasm-dataset}
# load post-only data
data_wsb2022_sarcasm = read_csv("./data/wsb_2022_postonly_sarcasm.csv")
# peek
data_wsb2022_sarcasm |>
  head(5)

# Derivate meaningful variables for descriptive & exploratory analysis
data = data_wsb2022_sarcasm |>
  # created time in NY timezone (wallstreet)
  dplyr::mutate(
    created_ny_time = format(
      lubridate::with_tz(lubridate::as_datetime(created, tz = "UTC"), tzone = "America/New_York"),
      "%H:%M:%S"
    ),
    created_ny_hour_bin = {
      ny_hour = as.integer(substr(created_ny_time, 1L, 2L))
      hour_label = dplyr::if_else(
        is.na(ny_hour), NA_character_, paste0(ny_hour, "-", (ny_hour + 1L) %% 24L)
      )
      factor(hour_label, levels = paste0(0:23, "-", (1:24) %% 24), ordered = TRUE)
    },
    # posts without body
    no_body = is.na(body) | trimws(body) == "",
    # post content word count
    body_work_count = stringr::str_count(dplyr::coalesce(body, ""), "\\S+"),
    # posts with only a link
    link_only = {
      body_text = stringr::str_trim(dplyr::coalesce(body, ""))
      (stringr::str_detect(body_text, "(?i)^https?://\\S+$") |
        stringr::str_detect(body_text, "(?i)^\\[[^\\]]+\\]\\(https?://\\S+\\)$")) &
        !stringr::str_detect(
          body_text,
          "(?i)https?://(?:[a-z0-9-]+\\.)*(?:reddit\\.com|redd\\.it)(?=[:/?#]|$)"
        )
    }
  )

# peek
data |>
  head(5) |>
  kable()

colnames(data)
```

## data removed

**Child Comment Filtering (~1,002,830 rows dropped)**: The raw scraped dataset contained over 1.09 million items. Over 90% of these records represent child comment replies (where title == "Comment"). Because our research goal is predicting thread-level submission engagement (comms_num), child comment replies lack independent comment totals and post titles. Retaining them would severely bias target metrics. Restricting analysis strictly to top-level submissions reduced the working dataset to ~96,375 records. 

Corrupted Identifier Records (1,114 rows dropped): Programmatic verification identified 1,114 rows lacking valid submission IDs (id == NA). These corrupted rows were dropped during initial pipeline filtering.  

Missing Creation Timestamps (51 rows dropped): Quality assertions flagged 51 rows where the post creation timestamp was missing (created == NA). Because creation timestamps are strictly required to engineer our temporal market-hour features (created_ny_hour_bin), these incomplete records were removed.

Missing Sarcasm Scores (11 rows dropped): Quality assertions identified 11 records lacking valid title_sarcasm scores. These missing values occurred during natural language processing (NLP) batch inference due to special characters or non-UTF-8 text encoding. Because title sarcasm is our central independent variable, these 11 rows were removed. 

Zero Imputation for Missing Engagement (comms_num): Rather than discarding submissions with missing comment counts, missing comms_num values were imputed to 0 via coalesce(), correctly representing posts that received zero user replies.   Following this pipeline, the final cleaned dataset contains 95,199 verified top-level submissions with zero missing values across critical modeling features**


# Descriptive analysis and missing data
```{r}
# Load assertion library
if (!requireNamespace("assertr", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("assertr")
library(assertr)

# 1. Clean missing IDs and target values
data_cleaned = data |>
  filter(!is.na(id), !is.na(created)) |> # Remove rows without an ID or timestamp
  mutate(comms_num = dplyr::coalesce(comms_num, 0)) # Replace NA comment counts with 0

# 2. Run quality assertions
data_verified = data_cleaned |>
  verify(comms_num >= 0) |> # Engagement counts must be non-negative
  verify(!is.na(id)) |> # Reddit Post IDs must not be NA
  verify(!is.na(created)) |> # Timestamps must exist
  verify(!is.na(title_sarcasm) & title_sarcasm >= 0 & title_sarcasm <= 100) |>
  verify(!is.na(body_sarcasm) & body_sarcasm >= 0 & body_sarcasm <= 100)

# 3. Document dataset dimensions
dim_source = dim(data_wsb2022_sarcasm)
dim_filtered = dim(data_verified)

dim_summary = tibble(
  Stage = c("Post-only Source Dataset", "Cleaned & Verified Dataset"),
  Rows = c(dim_source[1], dim_filtered[1]),
  Columns = c(dim_source[2], dim_filtered[2])
)

dim_summary |> kable(caption = "Dataset Dimensions Before and After Cleaning")
```

## data summary

```{r column-summaries}
# 1. Structural summary of all columns (types and sample values)
dplyr::glimpse(data_verified)

# 2. Standard summary, excluding the Unix timestamp
summary(data_verified |> select(-created))

# 3. Detailed summary statistics table for numeric features
data_verified |>
  select(where(is.numeric), -created) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") |>
  group_by(Variable) |>
  summarise(
    Min = min(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1 = quantile(Value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3 = quantile(Value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Std_Dev = sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(Variable = dplyr::recode(
    Variable,
    score = "Post score",
    comms_num = "Comment count",
    title_sarcasm = "Title sarcasm score (0–100)",
    body_sarcasm = "Body sarcasm score (0–100)",
    body_work_count = "Body word count",
    .default = Variable
  )) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c(
      "Measure", "Minimum", "1st quartile", "Median", "Mean",
      "3rd quartile", "Maximum", "Std. deviation"
    ),
    caption = "Summary Statistics for Numeric Variables"
  )
```

### Posts by New York hour

```{r hour-bin-summary}
data_verified |>
  count(created_ny_hour_bin, name = "Posts", .drop = FALSE) |>
  arrange(created_ny_hour_bin) |>
  mutate(Share = 100 * Posts / sum(Posts)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 1,
    col.names = c("New York hour", "Post count", "Share (%)"),
    caption = "Posts by New York Local Hour"
  )
```

### Link-only bodies

```{r link-only-summary}
data_verified |>
  count(link_only, name = "Posts") |>
  mutate(
    link_only = if_else(link_only, "Yes", "No"),
    Share = 100 * Posts / sum(Posts)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 1,
    col.names = c("Link-only body", "Post count", "Share (%)"),
    caption = "Posts with Link-Only Bodies"
  )
```

### Missing bodies

```{r no-body-summary}
data_verified |>
  count(no_body, name = "Posts") |>
  mutate(
    no_body = if_else(no_body, "Yes", "No"),
    Share = 100 * Posts / sum(Posts)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 1,
    col.names = c("Body missing", "Post count", "Share (%)"),
    caption = "Posts with Missing Bodies"
  )
```


# Exploratory data analysis



```{r plot-target-and-predictor-distributions, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# Target Variable: Raw vs. Log-Transformed Engagement
p1 = ggplot(data_verified, aes(x = comms_num)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#2b5c8f", color = "black", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title = "Raw Comment Count (Log Y-Scale)", x = "comms_num", y = "Count (Log Scale)") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 = ggplot(data_verified, aes(x = log1p(comms_num))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#2e7d32", color = "black", alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Log Target: log(1 + comms_num)", x = "log1p(comms_num)", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

#  Pairwise Scatterplot & Density Matrix
if (!requireNamespace("GGally", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("GGally")
library(GGally)

matrix_vars = data_verified |>
  mutate(
    log_comms = log1p(as.numeric(comms_num)),
    log_score = log1p(as.numeric(score)),
    log_words = log1p(as.numeric(body_work_count)),
    title_sarcasm = as.numeric(title_sarcasm)
  ) |>
  select(log_comms, title_sarcasm, log_score, log_words)

ggpairs(
  matrix_vars,
  columnLabels = c("Log Comms", "Sarcasm", "Log Score", "Log Words"),
  lower = list(continuous = wrap("points", alpha = 0.03, size = 0.3, color = "#2c3e50")),
  diag = list(continuous = wrap("densityDiag", fill = "#3498db", alpha = 0.5)),
  upper = list(continuous = wrap("cor", size = 4, color = "black"))
) + theme_minimal()

#  Scatterplots with Non-Linear Smoothing Curves
p_sarcasm = ggplot(data_verified, aes(x = as.numeric(title_sarcasm), y = log1p(as.numeric(comms_num)))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.03, color = "#1a237e", size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", color = "#d32f2f", size = 1.2, se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Sarcasm Probability vs. Log Engagement",
    x = "Title Sarcasm Score",
    y = "Log Engagement log(1 + comms_num)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_score = ggplot(data_verified, aes(x = log1p(as.numeric(score)), y = log1p(as.numeric(comms_num)))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.03, color = "#004d40", size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#ff6f00", size = 1.2, se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Log Upvote Score vs. Log Engagement",
    x = "Log Upvotes log(1 + score)",
    y = "Log Engagement log(1 + comms_num)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_sarcasm + p_score
```

## comments from graphs

- Upvote count exhibits a strong positive linear relationship with comment volume.
- Linear correlation between sarcasm and log comments is near zero, however a nonlinear colleration can be see. there is a small peak as sarcasm score between a score of 0 and ~15 and then a dip until 25. 
- Relation with Post Length & Upvotes: Word count has a moderate negative correlation with upvotes

## features that may undermine analysis / missing features

- Upvote score shares a strong correlation with comment count, however, comments can me made after the dataset was created. 
- Title sarcasm probability exhibits a near-zero linear correlation with comments. Linear modeling will fail to capture this tends
- The analysis models can not account for sarcasm in replies as those were discarded
- Both comms_num and score have extremely long tails (max score 22,503 vs. median about 80).
- Emoji and Reddit emote markup appear in the data. Sarcasm cues in WSB are often carried by emoji which text-only methods will not properly handle.
